To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the biosynthesis of nucleic acids and lipids during recovery of heat-injured cells was not inhibited by the addition of chloramphenicol.
The biosynthesis of DNA, RNA, and lipids is enhanced during the first 2 hours of recovery from heat injury, while protein synthesis is inhibited.
heat shock proteins are produced in response to heat shock and that the synthesis of these proteins is controlled by heat shock genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biosynthesis of macromolecular components during recovery from heat inactivation of Salmonella typhimirum.
the synthesis of new compounds from existing ones and their subsequent reactions.
the synthesis of the major components of the cell and the relationship of this synthesis to the recovery from injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the biosynthetic activity in S. typhimurim 7136 during recovery from heat shock is directed toward nucleic acids, lipid, and pool material, but not toward protein.

there is a marked decrease in the incorporation of label into nucleic acids and pool material, and a decrease of 60 to 75% in the incorporation of 14C label into lipid during the early stages of recovery.
there was a marked inhibition of biosynthesis in heat-injured S. typhimurim, with the exception of the biosynthesis of nucleic acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the synthesis of nucleic acids and the turnover of pool material are important for recovery from heat injury in S. typhimurim 7136.

the biosynthesis during recovery is not a simple reflection of the biosynthetic activities of the normal cells, but that the biosynthetic pathways are altered in a manner consistent with the observed changes in membrane permeability.
the heat injury process in S. typhimururium is a very complex process that is not fully understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are two different types of heat shock responses.
there is no evidence of a specific protein that is required for recovery of heat injury, at least not in the first 2 hours after heating.
we need to be aware of the fact that the recovery of heat-injured bacteria is a dynamic process.
